EyeTest.IntroSub: A quick 3-part screening to help identify potential refractive errors and colour vision.
EyeTest.OneHandBanner: Cover one eye with your free hand — you'll only need your other thumb to tap through each step.
EyeTest.IntroAcuityDesc: Cover one eye at a time and tap where the gap is on each of {{count}} rings. No time limit.
EyeTest.IntroColorDesc: Identify numbers hidden in coloured dot plates (Ishihara-style).
EyeTest.IntroAstigmatismDesc: View a radial pattern to detect uneven focus in the eye.
EyeTest.IntroDisclaimer: This is a preliminary screening only and does not replace a professional eye examination by a qualified optometrist.
EyeTest.AcuityPurpose: Measures how much fine detail your eye can resolve — the sharpness of your sight. Trouble here often points to short- or long-sightedness.
EyeTest.AcuityStep1: Cover one eye with your free hand — each eye is tested on its own.
EyeTest.AcuityStep2: Hold the phone at arm's length and look at the small broken ring (a “C”).
EyeTest.AcuityStep3: Tap the spot on the big ring below where you saw the gap.
EyeTest.AcuityStep4: You'll do this {{count}} times per eye. Get one right and the next ring shrinks; get one wrong and it grows back.
EyeTest.AcuityNote: There's no timer — take as long as you need on each ring.
EyeTest.ColorPurpose: Checks how well you tell colours apart, especially reds and greens. This is an Ishihara-style test, the standard screen for colour vision deficiency.
EyeTest.ColorStep1: Both eyes stay open for this one — nothing to cover.
EyeTest.ColorStep2: Each plate is a circle of coloured dots with a number hidden inside.
EyeTest.ColorStep3: Tap the number you can see. If no number stands out, tap “{{nothing}}”.
EyeTest.ColorStep4: Keep your screen brightness up and avoid strong coloured lighting.
EyeTest.ColorNote: Answer with your first impression — guessing at a blurry plate is fine, and there is no timer.
EyeTest.AstigmatismPurpose: Looks for an unevenly curved cornea, which makes some directions focus more sharply than others. It shows up as lines that look darker or blurrier in one direction.
EyeTest.AstigmatismStep1: Cover one eye with your free hand — again, one eye at a time.
EyeTest.AstigmatismStep2: Hold the phone at arm's length and look at the centre dot of the fan.
EyeTest.AstigmatismStep3: Let your eyes relax and notice the spokes with your side vision.
EyeTest.AstigmatismStep4: Tell us whether all the lines look equally sharp, or some stand out.
EyeTest.AstigmatismNote: Some lines looking bolder than others is exactly what this test is designed to catch — answer honestly.
EyeTest.CoverSubLeft: Cover your right eye with your free hand. When you're ready, we'll test your left eye only.
EyeTest.CoverSubRight: Cover your left eye with your free hand. When you're ready, we'll test your right eye only.
EyeTest.CoverBannerLeft: Keep the phone at arm's length and tap Continue once your right eye is covered.
EyeTest.CoverBannerRight: Keep the phone at arm's length and tap Continue once your left eye is covered.
EyeTest.AcuityCoverLeft: Cover your <bold>right</bold> eye with your free hand, then read with your left eye only.
EyeTest.AcuityCoverRight: Cover your <bold>left</bold> eye with your free hand, then read with your right eye only.
EyeTest.AcuityInstruction: Hold the phone at arm's length. Find the gap in the ring below — take as long as you need.
EyeTest.AcuityQuestion: Tap the spot on the ring below where you saw the gap.
EyeTest.AstigmatismCoverLeft: Cover your <bold>right</bold> eye with your free hand, hold the phone at arm's length.
EyeTest.AstigmatismCoverRight: Cover your <bold>left</bold> eye with your free hand, hold the phone at arm's length.
EyeTest.AstigmatismInstruction: Look at the center dot of the pattern below. Keep your eyes relaxed.
EyeTest.AstigmatismQuestion: Do all the lines appear equally dark and the same thickness?
EyeTest.PlateHintTwoDigit: A two-digit number is hidden among the dots.
EyeTest.PlateHintOneDigit: A single digit is concealed in the pattern.
EyeTest.ColorFooter: This is a self-reported screening. Results may vary with screen brightness and ambient lighting.
EyeTest.RiskLowSummary: Your vision appears healthy based on this screening.
EyeTest.RiskLowAdvice: No immediate concerns detected. Routine annual check-ups are still recommended to keep your eyes healthy.
EyeTest.RiskMediumSummary: Some signs of a possible refractive error were detected.
EyeTest.RiskMediumAdvice: We recommend a professional eye examination within the next 1–3 months. An optometrist can confirm and prescribe the right correction.
EyeTest.RiskHighSummary: Significant signs of refractive error were detected.
EyeTest.RiskHighAdvice: Please book an appointment with our optometrist as soon as possible. Early correction prevents further deterioration.
EyeTest.SpecialistText: If you have an eye condition and need to see a specialist, please submit a request below. A referral is necessary for a specialist appointment, which you can obtain from your General Practitioner or Optometrist.
EyeTest.AcuityAllClear: Both eyes read the chart clearly.
EyeTest.AcuityDifficulty: One or both eyes had difficulty reading the smaller lines.
EyeTest.ColorDeficient: Signs of colour vision deficiency detected.
EyeTest.AstigmatismOk: All lines appeared equally dark and clear — no irregularity detected.
EyeTest.AstigmatismNotOk: Some lines appeared darker or thicker than others.
EyeTest.ResultFooter: Results are indicative only. A full clinical eye examination by a licensed optometrist is required for a prescription.
